summary: First iteration: full backend regression (19 pytest tests) + focused Playwright UI sweep of login, dashboard, assets, maintenance kanban, logout. 18/19 backend tests pass; 1 fails: brute-force lockout does not trigger reliably behind the ingress. Frontend flows all pass with the specified data-testids.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout never returns 429. The identifier used is `f"{request.client.host}:{email}"` — behind the k8s ingress there are multiple upstream pods, so login_attempts get split across 2+ identifiers (10.208.128.9:... and 10.208.128.10:...) and no single row hits count>=5. Verified in DB. Also, TrustedHost/ForwardedFor is not applied — the app never sees the real client IP anyway, so this control is effectively bypassable.

minor.issue: CORSMiddleware is configured with allow_origins=['*'] AND allow_credentials=True. Browsers reject credentialed responses with wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin. It currently works because frontend and backend share the same origin (same host through ingress), but any deployment where they differ will break cookie auth. Should echo the request Origin explicitly (use FRONTEND_URL env).

On every failed attempt the code overwrites `locked_until` to `now + 15min`, which means the timer never truly locks (window is continuously reset but count keeps growing). Better to only set locked_until when count crosses the 5-threshold.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout: use only email (not IP) as identifier, or extract client IP from X-Forwarded-For. Only set locked_until when count reaches 5. Currently 429 is never returned to the client.
Tighten CORS: when allow_credentials=True, do not use allow_origins=['*']; instead set allow_origins=[FRONTEND_URL] (env var already present).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~1030 lines — consider splitting into routers/{auth,assets,allocation,booking,maintenance,org}.py for maintainability (soft limit is 700).
Brute-force identifier depends on request.client.host which is the ingress upstream, not the real client. Add a proxy-aware IP extractor or key on email only.
Locked_until is refreshed on every failed attempt, defeating a fixed lockout window.

Bookings query uses `start_at_dt`/`end_at_dt` datetime fields, but only start_at_dt is indexed — the overlap query would benefit from a compound (asset_id, status) index (partially covered by existing (asset_id, start_at_dt) index).
`get_current_user` accepts both a JWT access token and an Emergent session_token via `Authorization: Bearer` — this is a subtle overload; consider distinguishing the two paths explicitly.
test_credentials: admin@assetflow.io/admin123, manager@assetflow.io/manager123, head@assetflow.io/head123, employee@assetflow.io/employee123 — verified working via /api/auth/login.
seed_data_creation: Backend auto-seeds 4 users, 3 departments, 5 categories, 6 assets, plus sample allocation/maintenance/activity on startup. Verified via /api/dashboard/stats returning 9 total assets (6 seeded + 3 from tests).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression lives at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py. Only failing test is TestAuth::test_brute_force_lockout — root cause is IP-partitioned counter behind k8s ingress; fix requires changing the identifier logic in POST /api/auth/login. All other 18 tests (auth, RBAC, org, assets, allocation/transfer, booking overlap, maintenance lifecycle, dashboard, activity, notifications) pass consistently. Frontend Playwright coverage: /login → /dashboard, sidebar (app-sidebar), 6 dashboard cards, global-search-input, /assets table + Register dialog (created asset visible), /maintenance kanban 5 columns, user-menu-trigger → logout-button. Not yet exercised via UI: allocation/transfer flow, booking timeline, RBAC UI hiding for employees.
rca of the issue: brute-force lockout: `identifier = f'{request.client.host}:{email}'`. k8s ingress forwards to multiple backend replicas each with a distinct upstream source IP (10.208.128.9 and .10 observed in login_attempts collection). Failed attempts are hashed to whichever pod handled the request. After 5 failures the counter on pod A is 5, but the next attempt lands on pod B (count=0-3) and returns 401 instead of 429. Reproduce: register a fresh user, send 6 wrong logins in quick succession, observe all 401. Mitigation: key the counter on email only, or trust X-Forwarded-For and use the last hop client IP. Also stop refreshing locked_until every failure — set it only once when count hits threshold.
